variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
x = 10

# Variables can be rebound
x = 20

# Pattern matching binds variables
{a, b} = {1, 2}

# Pin operator prevents rebinding
^x = 20 # Match succeeds
variables.notes: Elixir data is immutable. Variables can be rebound to new values. The `=` operator is for pattern matching; use `^` to match against existing values.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
i = 42
f = 3.14
atom = :ok
tuple = {:person, "Alice", 30}
list = [1, 2, 3]
binary = <<"hello">>
string = "UTF-8 Binary"
pid = self()
data_types.notes: Elixir shares Erlang's type system. Strings are UTF-8 binaries. Atoms (symbols starting with `:`) are constants.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
add = 5 + 3
sub = 5 - 3
mul = 5 * 3
div_float = 5 / 2
div_int = div(5, 2)
rem_int = rem(5, 2)

# Strict boolean operators
logic = true and false or true

eq = 5 === 5 # Strict
neq = 5 !== 3
operators.notes: Boolean operators `and`, `or`, `not` require booleans. Relaxed operators `&&`, `||`, `!` allow truthy/falsy values (nil/false are falsy).

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
res = if x > 0 do
  "Positive"
else
  "Non-positive"
end

# Case with pattern matching
sign = case x do
  n when n > 0 -> 1
  n when n < 0 -> -1
  0 -> 0
end

# Cond
cond do
  x > 0 -> 1
  true -> 0
end
conditionals.notes: `cond` checks multiple conditions. `case` strictly uses pattern matching. `if/else` is a macro for a basic case.

for_loop.title: For Loop (Comprehensions)
for_loop.code:
# List comprehension
squares = for x <- [1, 2, 3, 4], do: x * x

# Filtering
evens = for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x

# Map
mapped = Enum.map([1, 2, 3], fn x -> x * 2 end)
for_loop.notes: Iteration is functional. `for` comprehensions are powerful macros. The `Enum` module provides all common collection operations.

while_loop.title: While Loop (Recursion)
while_loop.code:
defmodule Loop do
  def count(0), do: :ok
  def count(n) do
    IO.puts(n)
    count(n - 1)
  end
end

# GenServer state loop concept
# Processes recurse on receive to maintain state
while_loop.notes: Elixir has no loop constructs. State changes are driven by tail-recursive function calls, particularly in concurrent actors (GenServers).

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
defmodule Math do
  def add(x, y), do: x + y
  
  # Pattern matching
  def fact(0), do: 1
  def fact(n) when n > 0, do: n * fact(n - 1)
end

# Anonymous functions
multiply = fn x, y -> x * y end
short = &(&1 * &2)
functions.notes: Named functions live in modules. `&` enables terse anonymous functions. Pipe operator `|>` chains function calls natively.

arrays.title: Lists and Tuples
arrays.code:
list = [1, 2, 3]
new_list = [0 | list] # Fast prepend
concat = [1, 2] ++ [3, 4]

# Tuple
point = {10, 20}
first = elem(point, 0) # 0-indexed
arrays.notes: Lists are linked lists (slow random access, fast prepend). Tuples are contiguous memory (fast reads, expensive updates).

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
map = %{"name" => "Alice", :age => 30}

# Insert/Update (all keys)
map1 = Map.put(map, :city, "London")

# Update existing atom keys only
map2 = %{map1 | age: 31}

# Pattern matching
%{age: age} = map2
maps.notes: Maps are the go-to key-value structure. Atom keys allow shorthand syntax `%{key: val}`. `%{map | key: val}` updates strictly existing keys.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
# Result tuples
case File.read("file.txt") do
  {:ok, body} -> body
  {:error, reason} -> IO.puts("Error: #{reason}")
end

# Try/Rescue
try do
  1 / 0
rescue
  ArithmeticError -> 0
end
error_handling.notes: Idiomatic Elixir returns `{:ok, val}` or `{:error, reason}` tuples. Exceptions (`raise`, `rescue`) are reserved for truly unexpected crashes.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
# Single-line comment in Elixir
@doc """
Documentation for function
"""
def add(a, b), do: a + b
comments.notes: Elixir uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Elixir supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.code:
is_active = true
result = is_active and not false
booleans.notes: Elixir treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Elixir performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Elixir represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Elixir formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
case response do
  {:ok, data} -> IO.puts("Received #{data}")
  {:error, reason} -> IO.puts("Error: #{reason}")
end
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Elixir, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Elixir constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code: for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x * x
iterators.notes: Elixir achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.code:
defmodule Person do
  defstruct [:name, :age]
  def greet(%Person{name: name}), do: "Hello #{name}"
end
oop_classes.notes: Elixir emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Elixir are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Elixir uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Elixir provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
defmodule MyModule do
  import Enum, only: [map: 2]
  alias MyProject.Helper
end
modules_import.notes: Elixir isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
